caiu em minhas mãos um Itautec I-7000-G do começo dos anos 80
a ROM é de outubro de 1985, mas o modelo de computador se nao me engano entrou no mercado por volta de 1982 ou algo assim...

alguns anos atrás eu cheguei a escrever um rascunho de emulador pra esse computador no MAME usando os dumps de ROM que um cara chamado Alexandre Tabajara tinha feito e postado em algum site, acho que no datassette
meu emulador ficou meia boca por que eu não tinha acesso a detalhes das placas
nem esquematicos, nem manual de serviço, nem sequer fotos das PCBs. Nada!
Na cerdade cheguei a achar uma foto dessas de revista em que dava pra ver uma das placas. Mas era numa resolução terrivelmente baixa. Ajudou, mas ajudou pouco.
o emulador foi rascunhado na base dos chutes
chutes direcionados, experimentando coisas tipixas do design de computadores daquela época e vendo se a ROM lidava bem nesses ambientes simulados de hardware especulativos
foi o suficiente pra funcionar meia boca

tudo empoerado!
"TELEX"
Achei ovos e peles de lagartixa dentro do gabinete

em varios lugares, como nesse canto, tem umas cacas brancas que acho que são cagadinhas das lagartixas. Fiquei com muito nojo e medo de pegar alguma doenca! Talvez eu esteja muito impactado pelas notícias da China...
tirei um pouco da poeira de cima dos chips pra conseguir ler os códigos e tirei mais umas fotos
Essa é a placa do meio. Também não sei o que ela faz. Mas acho que deve ser a interface com os drives de disquete
também toda empoeirada e cheia de aranhas mortas

Depois de tirar a placa do meio, desaparafusei a chama de metal que serve de suporte para essas primeiras duas placas e para a fonte de alimentaćão e despluquei alguns cabos para tirar essas coisas do caminho e acessar a placa-mãe grandona que fica embaixo de tudo
descobri que o único jeito de soltar a placa grande é retirando o teclado
então eu primeiro tirei a tampa do teclado
e depois tirei 6 parafusos que o seguravam no lugar e retirei o teclado também
debaixo do teclado tinha essa chapa de metal. Tive que a desaparafusar e remover também
tá aqui o teclado solto. E embaixo dela tá o gabinete dos drives de disquete, que eu nem abri ainda
e aqui, finalmente, a placa-mãe inteira acessível, mas ainda aparafusada no fundo do gabinete

Criando uma placa de fliperama para a obra prima de Eric Chahi


Neste vídeo descrevo um apanhado de diversas idéias ao redor do plano mirabolante de criar uma placa de fliperama para rodar o jogo Another World, de Eric Chahi, do início da década de 1990.

Links para mais informações:
* Meu post sobre a VM no Fórum Fiozera: https://forum.fiozera.com.br/t/estudando-a-maquina-virtual-do-jogo-another-world/127
* Documentário sobre Eric Chahi e o desenvolvimento do jogo: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J0gv2bV9ok4
* VM implementada pelo Fabien Sanglard: https://github.com/fabiensanglard/Another-World-Bytecode-Interpreter
* Fabien Sanglard no Twitter: https://twitter.com/fabynou
* Oficinas de Retroprogramação no Garoa Hacker Clube: https://garoa.net.br/wiki/Retroprogramação
* Postagem de 2014 no meu blog em inglês: https://mamedev.emulab.it/fsanches/2014/12/13/another-world-bytecode-disassembly/
* Meu tweet de 2016 sobre a emulação do Another World no MAME: https://twitter.com/juca_gnu/status/686597622417719296
* Placa de desenvolvimento de FPGA Lattice iCEstick iCE40: https://www.embarcados.com.br/lattice-icestick-ice40/
* Artigo do Hackaday sobre o toolchain livre para FPGAs IceStorm: https://hackaday.com/2015/12/29/32c3-a-free-and-open-source-verilog-to-bitstream-flow-for-ice40-fpgas/
* Placa de desenvolvimento de FPGA NandLand Go-Board: https://www.nandland.com/goboard/introduction.html
* Atividade CPU do Zero do Garoa Hacker Clube: https://garoa.net.br/wiki/CPU_do_Zero
* Projeto de placa JAMMA para o jogo Another World: https://garoa.net.br/wiki/AnotherWorld_JAMMA
* Toolchain para a VM do jogo Another World: https://github.com/felipesanches/AnotherWorld_VMTools
* Exemplo "bounce": https://github.com/felipesanches/AnotherWorld_VMTools/blob/master/example/bounce.asm
* Exemplo "pong": https://github.com/felipesanches/AnotherWorld_VMTools/blob/master/example/pong.asm
* Livro "How to Design & Build Your Own Custom TV Games", David L. Heiserman, 1978: https://garoa.net.br/wiki/Custom_TV_Games
* Atari GranTrak 10: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R014taK2pZM
* Livro "Designing Video Game Hardware in Verilog", Steven Hugg, 2018: https://www.goodreads.com/book/show/43257510-designing-video-game-hardware-in-verilog

Happy Hacking!
Felipe "Juca" Sanches

text.text: The Computer Scientist Responsible for Cut, Copy, and Paste, Has Passed Away

texts.text: The advent of the personal computer wasn’t just about making these powerful machines available to everyone, it was also about making them accessible and usable, even for those lacking a computer science degree.

, who passed away on Monday, might not be a household name like Steve Jobs or Bill Gates, but his contributions to making computers and mobile devices easier to use are the highlight of a long career influencing modern computing.
Born in 1945 in New York, Tesler went on to study computer science at Stanford University, and after graduation he dabbled in artificial intelligence research (long before it became a

) and became involved in the anti-war and anti-corporate monopoly movements, with companies like IBM as one of his deserving targets. In 1973 Tesler took a job at the Xerox Palo Alto Research Center (PARC) where he worked until 1980. Xerox PARC is famously known for developing the mouse-driven graphical user interface we now all take for granted, and during his time at the lab Tesler worked with Tim Mott to create a word processor called Gypsy that is best known for coining the terms “cut,” “copy,” and “paste” when it comes to commands for removing, duplicating, or repositioning chunks of text.

text.text: Xerox PARC is also well known for not capitalizing on the groundbreaking research it did in terms of personal computing, so in 1980 Tesler transitioned to Apple Computer where he worked until 1997. Over the years he held countless positions at the company including Vice President of AppleNet (Apple’s in-house local area networking system that was eventually canceled), and even served as Apple’s Chief Scientist, a position that at one time was held by Steve Wozniak, before eventually leaving the company.

texts.text: In addition to his contributions to some of Apple’s most famous hardware, Tesler was also known for his efforts to make software and user interfaces more accessible. In addition to the now ubiquitous “cut,” “copy,” and “paste” terminologies, Tesler was also an advocate for an approach to UI design known as modeless computing, which is reflected in his

. In essence, it ensures that user actions remain consistent throughout an operating system’s various functions and apps. When they’ve opened a word processor, for instance, users now just automatically assume that hitting any of the alphanumeric keys on their keyboard will result in that character showing up on-screen at the cursor’s insertion point. But there was a time when word processors could be switched between multiple modes where typing on the keyboard would either add characters to a document or alternately allow functional commands to be entered.

text.text: There are still plenty of software applications where tools and functionality change depending on the mode they’re in (complex apps like Photoshop, for example, where various tools behave differently and perform very distinct functions) but for the most part modern operating systems like Apple’s macOS and Microsoft’s Windows have embraced user-friendliness through a less complicated modeless approach.

texts.text: After leaving Apple in 1997, Tesler co-founded a company called Stagecast Software which developed applications that made it easier and more accessible for children to learn programming concepts. In 2001 he joined Amazon and eventually became the VP of Shopping Experience there, in 2005 he switched to Yahoo where he headed up that company’s user experience and design group, and then in 2008 he became a product fellow at 23andMe.
, Tesler left 23andMe in 2009 and from then on mostly focused on consulting work.

text.text: While there are undoubtedly countless other contributions Tesler made to modern computing as part of his work on teams at Xerox and Apple that may never come to light, his known contributions are immense. Tesler is one of the major reasons computer moved out of research centers and into homes.
